exact_missing_items: Package-based worktrees are preferred over per-node worktrees for scale; dependent nodes within the same package need defined lane/ordering rules
Orchestrator-managed worktrees must be visible in both Orchestrator page and Source Control view; they must be separated/partitioned from user/assistant-created worktrees
Source Control worktree view must partition worktrees as: 'Orchestrator Owned' vs 'Other'; 'Orchestrator Owned' must be further subdivided by feature seam

Source Control / Worktree Handshake research findings: Source Control is the primary operational surface for worktree inventory and user actions; Orchestrator consumes worktree identity/ownership/blocked state/lineage for run/history/recovery views
Existing docs still describe ownership as run/tier/subtask worktrees which collides with the package-based lane-pool model
Recommended boundary: Orchestrator owns package lane-pool operational truth; Source Control owns repo/worktree execution and inspection operations — this is the canonical surface division
'lane' object required fields: project/package linkage, worktree binding, lifecycle, contamination state, safe-point linkage, ancestry, ownership/display grouping
Cleanup and restore semantics must be lane-aware; contamination scope and safe-point prerequisites are underspecified and must be resolved

Lane is the primary operational object in Orchestrator; Worktree is the concrete filesystem/Git backing for a lane instance — lane identity persists after the live worktree is cleaned up/archived/removed

Lane/worktree lifecycle vocabulary must include these states: baseline, active, suspect, restoring, retained, cleanup_eligible, archived, removed, historical; 'historical' coexists with 'archived' or 'removed'; 'cleanup_eligible' ≠ already removed
